### Sol-first jobs (superseding owner amendment, 2026-09-07)

Issue #301 comment5573256033 supersedes the earlier cleanup-only whitelist.
Routine/bounded jobs default to exact `gpt-5.6-sol`/`ultra`, including routine
existing-statement proof work, build repairs and independent reviews. Main chooses
`--job-class hard|escalated|source_semantic|control_policy|hard_review` with an
explicit `--hardness-reason` for genuinely difficult or escalated Astra work.
New game/hypothesis/source-semantic decisions and control-policy reviews justify
Astra; Lean files, prover/reviewer roles, or missing historical samples alone do not.
Exact edit specifications remain appropriate for mechanical cleanup, not a universal
Sol gate. The historical C01/C02 audit is retained as evidence, not a role ceiling.

For a model change, create a new explicit-model external assignment with Ultra;
`dispatch.sh --resume` does not switch an existing thread's model. Link the
predecessor thread, assignment, worktree, checkpoint and cumulative budget.
Observed models are not inferred from a requested argument. Independent review
still binds a different session to the exact head and trusted prompt. Hard
control-policy review remains Astra.

At reviewed activation, main records one timestamp in
`MIPSTARRE_MODEL_POLICY_ACTIVATION_AT`. External dispatch records `new` or
`resume` automatically; historical pre-activation native tasks remain
`grandfathered`. Grandfathering requires actual pre-activation turn evidence,
not a caller label. Main is excluded.
`model_policy.py --ratio-registry results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl --activation-at
TIMESTAMP` reports the last 100 distinct new dispatches, plus separate cumulative
counts. Target 20:1 within 10:1..50:1; unknown observations are not invented,
later known observations resolve them, and contradictory observations stay unknown.
Zero Astra is not a measurable ratio. Record finite-prefix/availability deviations;
never add filler or delay necessary hard work to manufacture a ratio.

No live activation until normal CI, independent control-policy review, service
merge and an explicit new Sol/Ultra runtime observation. Catalog/CLI Ultra is not
provider-measured reasoning. External admission uses the worker caps in section 4.
Deploy the shim with its adjacent checked helper, never as a stale standalone
copy. Keep all normal
caller, declaration, statement-integrity, proof-debt, CI/review and merge gates.
Escalation preserves all accumulated attempts, time, work and historical evidence.

Eight roles, fixed (`DESIGN.md`, "Naming and identity conventions"):

`orc`, `prover`, `reviewer`, `simplifier`, `blueprint`, `splitter`, `scout`,
`mathfix`.

Sandbox defaults follow from what the role is allowed to change:

| Role | Default sandbox | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| `reviewer`, `scout` | `read-only` | a reader must not be able to edit what it reports on |
| all others | `workspace-write` | they exist to change the worktree |

`--sandbox` overrides the default; asking for a writable reviewer produces a
loud warning, because a reviewer that can fix what it found has reviewed its
own diff (§6). `danger-full-access` disables the codex sandbox entirely and
warns; it is never a default.

The persona for a role lives at `local/personas/<role>.md`, with one naming
exception: the role code `orc` maps to `local/personas/orchestrator.md`.
Until such a file is committed, `dispatch.sh` warns and falls back to a
one-line built-in frame — enough to run, not enough for load-bearing work.
The `mathfix` role is the source-statement repair lane governed by
`issues-prs.md` section 6: main selects Astra Ultra after the #26 availability report,
supplying cumulative per-gap budgets; historical Fable records remain in `owner-sessions.jsonl`.

## 3. Naming

```
<role>-<scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq>        e.g. prover-0042-20260830-01
```

- `scope` is the `--issue` argument normalized to `[a-z0-9-]`, at most 40
  characters. An argument containing any of `[ ] ~ ^ : ? * \` is **rejected**,
  not sanitized. This is the bracket-free naming invariant
  (`DESIGN.md` invariant 9): the parent repository traced a class of automation
  failures to `]` surviving from bracketed issue titles into generated branch
  names, and adopted the convention as the fix
  (`docs/pr_review_management.md:163`, `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124`).
  Rejecting rather than stripping keeps the session name, the branch name and
  the issue id referring to the same string.
- `seq` is a two-digit counter, allocated under
  `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/locks/session-seq.lock` by scanning *both*
  `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` and `results/telemetry/sessions/` — a
  session that crashed before its registry line was written still owns its
  number, because its capture file exists.
- Names are stable identifiers: they appear in the registry, in capture file
  names, in the `dispatcher` field of child sessions, and in `audits/` reports.
  Never reuse one.

### 4.1 Dispatch

# Protocol: issues and pull requests

Normative for the GitHub-backed issue and PR lifecycle and the automation in
`local/bin/`; read `local/protocols/meta.md` first. The repository is
`Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A`, and GitHub is the **single source of truth** for
issues, PRs, CI and review evidence, and merges; CI and reviews still *execute*
here and publish their results there. No active `issues/` or `prs/` tree, no
shadow record, no write-through cache, no offline mutation mode: a GitHub error
fails the operation, never a local success (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-01).

## 1. Records, names, tools

Issues and PRs are GitHub's, identified by their numbers — no zero-padded ids,
no frontmatter. Parent/child structure is the native sub-issue relation
(`POST …/issues/{parent}/sub_issues`), one parent per issue exactly as the
retired `parent:` scalar allowed; discussion is comments; labels come from the
repository (`list-labels`, paginated), so `local/labels.yml` is retired and a
label absent from GitHub is reported, never invented.
`pr_open.py --issue N` inherits only its explicit descriptive-label allowlist
from issue N, unions it with explicit `--label` values, and adds those labels
without removing existing PR labels. Scheduling, approval and owner-state
labels are never inherited. Before push, creation/adoption requires at least
one descriptive label, supplied explicitly, inherited, or already on the PR;
otherwise the command explains how the operator can classify the change.
GitHub still validates label existence; the allowlist is an inheritance policy,
not a replacement registry. Backfills use the same additive API and inspect
the actual change when the source issue itself is unlabeled. Briefs (the design record
per issue) live in `local/briefs/`: agent input, not lifecycle state.

Prerequisites between issues are **GitHub issue dependencies**
(`GET`/`POST …/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocked_by`), one edge per prerequisite.
The edge is retained even when the prerequisite closes, so reopening it restores the block.
A prerequisite carried by a pull request is the packet issue that PR closes. The
"Dependencies" bullets in an issue body are commentary on those edges, never
the record. A packet is **ready** when it is an open leaf of the tracker tree
and every issue blocking it is closed; `local/bin/ready_packets.py` computes
that list, and the operator launches lanes from it rather than from a
hand-kept order or a dependency table in a comment (EVOLUTION.md 2026-09-04).
Establish or adopt each edge with
`local/bin/gh_common.py add-blocked-by ISSUE PREREQUISITE`. The command first
reads the edge, makes at most one mutation, and re-reads after an ambiguous
failure; it is therefore safe to repeat. Record closed prerequisites too.

Every GitHub call goes through `local/bin/gh_common.py` — a module for Python
callers, and for the shell scripts a CLI (`pr-view`, `post-status`,
`latest-statuses`, `ensure-pr-comment`, `post-review`, `merge-pr`,
`issue-create`, `add-blocked-by`, `issue-close`, `snapshot`, …; `--help` lists
them) owning CLI discovery, repository resolution, API version headers,
bounded retry of transient failures and the exit-2-with-stderr convention.
Nothing else shells out to `gh`. `issue_new.py`, `issue_close.py`, `pr_open.py`,
`ci.sh`, `review.sh`, `autofix.sh`, `pr_merge.py`, `github-sync.sh` take GitHub
numbers; `track.py`, `validate_tree.py` and `export_issues.py` are deleted.

Every repository-owned branch publication runs through `checked-push.sh` with
one explicit `refs/heads/...:refs/heads/...` mapping.  The helper reads the
remote tip with a short `ls-remote`, resolves the local ref's registered
worktree, and refuses a checkout whose HEAD or working tree differs from the
captured commit.  It runs that checkout's `.githooks/pre-push` against the exact
ref tuple before starting `receive-pack`, then pushes the captured commit under
an exact remote-tip lease.  The native hook performs a short defense-in-depth
comparison when selected, while the helper's lease makes a moved remote ref fail
closed even when that hook is stale or absent.  A caller's explicit
`MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` remains the documented emergency bypass.  It skips
validation only: implicit tag following stays disabled, so publication remains
limited to the explicit branch mapping.

`github-sync.sh [ref ...]` takes branch names (default `main`), not a `push`
subcommand. It retains the post-publication record snapshot. When an explicitly
requested/default main push succeeded and the snapshot created a new telemetry
commit, it checked-pushes main once more without creating another snapshot.
Branch-only calls never implicitly publish main. Snapshot reads remain best-effort;
snapshot commit or final publication failure returns nonzero and leaves the
preserved local state for the operator to recover.

Every merge of `github/main` or a stack parent into an issue branch runs the
merge-loss guard before the merge commit is created. The guard compares the
pending index with `HEAD`, `MERGE_HEAD`, and every best merge base. It refuses
an incoming path that disappeared without a branch-side deletion and an
incoming-only entry restored wholesale to the unchanged branch blob. Paths
recorded by Git as conflicts remain resolution decisions. The
`reference-transaction` hook checks an automatic merge's commit object before
the branch ref moves; `pre-commit` checks the pending index for a merge
committed later. Neither path permits `MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS` to bypass this
check. A lane checking an existing merge uses the primary checkout's
`local/bin/merge_loss_guard.py --repo <worktree> --commit <merge>` so a stale
branch copy cannot weaken the audit.

* Branches: `issue-<github-number>-<slug>`, or `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>`
  from an agent; `pr_open.py` rejects what `git check-ref-format` would.
* Titles, slugs and branch names are **bracket-free**: bot-generated branch
  names inherit those characters and "`]` breaks part of the PR automation
  stack" (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124). A `:` in a *title* is fine
  (`Tracking: …`), but not in a branch.
* `autofix.sh`'s automated fix commits keep the exact subject prefixes
  `[codex-auto-fix]` and `[codex-review-fix]`; its iteration counter and the
  review skip key on them.  Operator and worker repairs use plain
  `fix(review): …` / `fix(ci): …` subjects so the reviewer sees them.
* `Closes #N` / `Fixes #N` auto-closes the issue on merge, `Addresses #N` does
  not (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:61-62) — and the numbers being GitHub's, that
  footer is now literally what GitHub itself reads.

## 2. Evidence contracts

All evidence binds to the **exact head SHA** (DESIGN.md invariant 2).

**Commit statuses.** Ten canonical contexts, posted by `post-status`: one
`local-ci/<step>` per CI step (`build`, `blueprint-render`, `paper-gaps`,
`blueprint-sync`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`,
`statement-origin`), plus `local-ci/summary` and `local-review/summary`.
`ci.sh` posts `pending` before each gate step and `success | failure | error`
after it; a gated-out step is a `success` saying it was skipped. The gate reads
the *latest* status per context (`latest-statuses`), never GitHub's combined
status, silent as that is about contexts never posted. The run manifest is one
PR comment marked `<!-- mipstarre-ci-manifest pr=N -->`, kept current by
`ensure-pr-comment`: evidence for humans, while the statuses are the gate.

**Review verdict.** One `COMMENT` review per head SHA, bound to `commit_id`,
carrying `<!-- mipstarre-review pr=N head=SHA -->`, the findings ledger, and the
line `VERDICT: APPROVED | COMMENTED | CHANGES_REQUESTED (code=…, prose=…)`.
Unchecked findings are ledger lines matching `^\s*[-*]\s*\[ \]`; clean means
`APPROVED`, or `COMMENTED` with none of them. Adverse verdicts post as `COMMENT`
too — a **single account** cannot approve its own pull request, so the review
event carries no authority — and adverseness travels in `local-review/summary`
(`failure` for unresolved findings), which is the gate's review evidence.

**Adjudication** (review.md §12) is a PR comment whose body starts with
`ADJUDICATION` and contains `head=<SHA>` for the current head, one disposition
line per remaining finding; `--adjudicated` takes nothing else.

**Idempotency.** Every publishing step is **at most one mutation**: a paginated
read finds the stable marker first and adopts that record instead of duplicating
it (`commentOnce`, issue-automation.yml:403-417, now guarding retries rather than
webhook redelivery); an ambiguous write stays pending for adoption.

## 3. The merge gate

`pr_merge.py <number>` is the only path to `main`: never `git merge` to main,
never push `main`. The merge is a REST `PUT …/pulls/{n}/merge` with the exact
`sha` guard, issued by `gh_common.merge_pr` and verified against the merge
commit's topology (two parents, the frozen head second), behind seven gates
that refuse by default:

1. the PR is open, unmerged and not a draft (`draft is False`, not merely
   falsy), and reports a head SHA, a head ref and a base ref;
2. the primary worktree is clean and on the base, and the local branch tip
   equals the GitHub head SHA — the merge must be of the bytes built here. After
   fetching the current GitHub base, the head is fresh when that base is its
   ancestor, or when every raw tree change from their merge base to the base is
   allowlisted passive telemetry: a regular non-executable (`100644`) `.md` or
   `.jsonl` file below `results/telemetry/`, or a generated regular
   non-executable `.json` file below the exact
   `results/telemetry/github-snapshot/` subtree. The check uses
   `git diff --raw -z --no-renames` so additions, deletions and both sides of a
   rename retain their paths and modes. Executable files, executable-mode
   changes, symlinks, code or unknown suffixes, malformed records, paths outside
   those boundaries, a missing merge base and every failed Git command block;
3. all eight `local-ci/<step>` contexts plus `local-ci/summary` are `success` on
   that exact SHA; a **missing** context blocks, because GitHub's combined state
   reads `success` for a commit carrying no statuses at all;
4. that SHA's marker-bound `COMMENT` review (or one carried forward per
   review.md §13) carries `VERDICT: APPROVED`, or
   `COMMENTED` with zero unchecked findings, **and** `local-review/summary` is
   `success` there;
5. no `CHANGES_REQUESTED` review stands on that head, from anyone;
6. no live fix lock for the branch (`locks/fix-<branch>.lock`, running holder);
   the count of `merge-base..head` commits whose subject starts with a §1 fix
   prefix is printed for the record and is not a gate;
7. every issue the PR body closes — all nine of GitHub's closing keywords, not
   just `Closes` — has no open sub-issue left.

`--adjudicated` waives gate 4's adverse verdict and nothing else, and only when
an exact-head `ADJUDICATION` comment backs it; gate 5 is never adjudicable.

Afterwards a best-effort, non-fatal tail fast-forwards local `main` to the
remote merge commit; branch and worktree cleanup keeps its safeguards (local
dirt defers it with a warning).

### Main-cycle integration checkpoint

The active owner service records, at each bounded tick, the local `main` SHA,
the readable remote `refs/heads/main` SHA, primary cleanliness, transport
result, and the age and exact head of the oldest CI-and-review-eligible open
PR. A dirty primary, remote mismatch, unavailable transport, active fix or
transaction lock, missing configured Space allocation or external-zero gate, or a stale
candidate is
a HOLD reason; it is never silently converted into a merge attempt. After a
successful daemon-owned merge, the service re-reads remote `main` and records
the new SHA before the next tick. The service may invoke `pr_merge.py` only as
its daemon-owned final action after these checks; workers never merge directly.
Each tick has bounded Git/GitHub reads and records failures as HOLD rather than
exiting the loop. The cadence is monotonic: work time is subtracted from the
configured interval (default 300 seconds). Candidate records distinguish stale
exact-head PRs from fresh actionable PRs using `pr_merge.head_is_fresh`, the
same conservative predicate as gate 2b; `pr_age_s` is PR creation age, while
eligibility onset remains unknown unless separately observed.

## 4. Untrusted text

Issue and PR bodies are untrusted data, and **more** so now that they arrive
from GitHub: anyone with repository access, and every imported external report,
writes the fields that are echoed into generated markdown and interpolated into
agent prompts. All three parent workflows sanitized before interpolation, and
`wf_util.sanitize` is that step ported: strip control characters, break fenced
code with zero-width spaces, truncate to 200 characters for titles and 5000 for
bodies (issue-automation.yml:122-128).

Every LLM hook in `local/bin` carries the same four requirements: gate on
`MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED != "false"`; read prompts from committed main
(`git show main:…`), never the branch under review (DESIGN.md:76-77); frame
sanitized text as data that must not be followed; and filter any model-proposed
label through the repository's label list. `audit_stale_issues.py` additionally
keeps its path-traversal rejection for externally sourced citations.

`MIPSTARRE_GH` is the path to `gh` (else `PATH`, else the documented user-local
location); `MIPSTARRE_GITHUB_REPO` overrides the `owner/name` otherwise read
from the `github` remote; `MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP` (default 5) bounds `autofix.sh`'s
own loop only — the merge gate does not read it — and is operator-tunable with

in the layer. `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` and
`LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` keep kill-switch semantics (DESIGN.md:73-75).

`github-sync.sh` pushes explicit refs and writes an atomic, paginated read-only

(`open-issues.json`, `open-pulls.json`, `metadata.json`; PRs filtered out of the

## 6. Owner inbox and mathematical-gap escalation

Pinned issue #26 is the owner inbox: it receives only decisions that require
the human owner. A source statement found to be mathematically false does not
go there first. Following the availability report on #26 and the September 6
owner decision, main selects Astra Ultra for the mathematical-gap lane through
`MIPSTARRE_CODEX_MODEL=gpt-6-astra local/bin/dispatch.sh --role mathfix --effort ultra`.
Historical owner-launched Fable measurements remain unchanged. Every request or
dispatch carries the exact source path, label and line range; the counterexample
or obstruction; the paper-gap note; the relevant blueprint dependency graph and
Lean consumers; and the cumulative session count and elapsed working time.

A correction is adopted only when it meets all four conditions below.

1. **Correctness:** the known counterexample no longer applies, adversarial
   checks find no replacement counterexample, and a mathematical proof sketch
   derives the corrected conclusion from its explicit hypotheses using cited
   source results.
2. **Sufficiency:** every use in the paper and every dependent node in the
   blueprint graph remains justified; checking only the first Lean consumer is
   insufficient.
3. **Minimality:** the correction is the closest sufficient statement to the
   source, with no unnecessary hypothesis or weakened conclusion and no change
   to the source semantics; definition or game corrections require an explicit
   faithfulness audit and independent mathematical review.
4. **Lean convergence:** the corrected statement type-checks and all affected
   downstream consumers compile. Lean success alone does not establish the
   preceding three conditions.

The operator iterates mathematics and Lean for at most ten `mathfix` sessions
or about one and a half working days per gap, whichever comes first. The budget
is shared across the historical owner-launched Fable lane and the Astra lane; a
model or telemetry change does not reset it. Main decides mathematical
corrections with the preceding evidence and independent review, including
definition/game corrections that preserve the intended source semantics;
changing the project goal is outside that authority. If the current authorized
budget expires, stop that lane and record the attempted statements,
counterexamples, proof sketches and unresolved consumers on #27 and in the gap
note. Do not reset attempts or working time. Use #26 only for an owner-only
permission, credential, access or scope/resource grant; mathematical difficulty
alone is not an owner decision. An already-posted #26 item waits for the owner
unless the owner explicitly returns it to main.

An adopted correction follows the ordinary CI and independent-review gates. The
operator announces it in one line on progress log #27 and records it in the
paper-gap note, `results/telemetry/events.md`, and
`results/telemetry/design-decisions.md`. That announcement informs the owner; it
is not a request for a decision.
# Build cache protocol — the hot main cache

Normative. This document specifies the local replacement for the parent
workflow's GitHub Actions build cache, and the rules every worktree must obey to
avoid duplicate compilation. It is the protocol behind three executables:

| script | role |
|---|---|
| `local/bin/cache-warmer.sh` | the **single writer**: builds `main`, publishes read-only snapshots |
| `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh` | the **consumer**: keyhash-gated copy-on-write clone into a worktree |
| `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` | fresh-worktree bootstrap (replaces `.codex/setup.sh`) |

Governing invariants: `local/DESIGN.md` #1 (single cache writer) and #7 (one full
`lake build` machine-wide). Where this document and `DESIGN.md` disagree,
`DESIGN.md` wins.

---

## 1. What is being replaced, and why it was built that way

The parent repository's caching design is the residue of a specific, documented
failure. The load-bearing citations:

| parent mechanism | citation | what it encodes |
|---|---|---|
| Split restore/save, save only on `main` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:137-167` | *"The cache is saved only from main and restored everywhere."* |
| `lean-action`'s own cache disabled | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:138-142` | The post-mortem: a ~2.6 GB entry saved **per PR run** cycled through the 10 GB repository cache budget and evicted the main-branch entry, *"so no run ever restored usable MIPStarRE oleans and every run rebuilt the whole library."* |
| Same policy restated in the weekly job | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:75-77` | *"See pr-ci.yml: per-run lake caches evict the main build cache from the repository cache budget."* |
| Main runs exempt from cancellation | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:50` | *"Do not cancel main-branch runs: they seed the build cache."* |
| Save runs `if: always()` on main | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:161-162` | *"Save even when the build failed: a partial cache still spares the next run the modules that did compile."* |
| ProofWidgets prune workaround | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:56-69` | A fresh-tree upstream bug that aborts the entire Mathlib cache fetch |
| `elan` install isolated from the cache lifecycle | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:44-54` | Avoids *"a partial cache save or restore-then-overwrite that could negate the ProofWidgets workaround"* |
| Independent cache for the doc subproject | `.github/workflows/docgen.yml:135-140` | `docbuild/` is its own Lake project with its own key |
| Mathlib bumps are manual only | `.github/workflows/update.yml:3-5` | A bump *"triggers a full library rebuild and possibly an auto-fix cascade"* |
| Lean setup removed from a PR job | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml:314` | A job was demoted to a notice *"after repeated runner disk exhaustion"* |

The single sentence to carry forward: **many writers destroyed the one valuable
cache entry.** Every rule below exists to make that impossible locally, where the
same failure mode reappears as parallel agent worktrees writing into a shared
build tree.

---

## 2. The two-tier split

`.lake/` holds two caches with different provenance, different lifetimes, and
different sharing rules. Conflating them is the primary way to reintroduce the
parent's failure.

An absolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` relocates `.lake` to `<root>/<branch>` for a
one-component branch name. The helper rejects `/`, symlink targets, escape, and
canonical overlap with packages, `hot-main`, the repository, or any worktree,
plus canonical-equal ownership by another worktree. Export it before setup or
warming and through dispatch and cleanup; only its target gets `--add-dir`.

**Tier 1 — `.lake/build`** — this project's own compiled artifacts (`.olean`,
`.ilean`, `.c`, `.trace` for `MIPStarRE` modules). This is *exactly* what the
parent cached, and only from `main`. Locally it is produced by the warmer and
distributed as copy-on-write clones. Each worktree owns a **private, writable**
copy.

**Tier 2 — `.lake/packages`** — Mathlib and its transitive dependencies. The
parent never put these in the GitHub cache; they come from Mathlib's own cloud
cache via `lake exe cache get` inside `lean-action`. Locally they live **once
per manifest** in a shared, read-only store:
`$CACHE_ROOT/packages/<key>`, `key = sha256(lake-manifest.json ‖ lean-toolchain)[:16]`,
and every worktree's `.lake/packages` is a symlink to it.

> **Why a shared store is safe here (2026-09-03).** The old objection — a
> shared tree is read-only only by convention, so one `lake update` mutates it
> for everyone — is answered mechanically: the store is `chmod -R a-w`, so any
> write (an automated `lake update`, a dependency rebuild after a manifest
> drift) fails loudly in the one worktree that attempted it. Identity is by
> key, so a Mathlib bump simply creates a new store entry; worktrees on the old
> manifest keep linking the old one. The first worktree to need a key fetches
> with `lake exe cache get` into a real directory, then *publishes* it (move,
> `chmod a-w`, link); later worktrees only link. Cost: 7.3 GB once per key
> instead of per worktree (8 copies = 58 GB on 2026-09-03, on a 97 % full disk).
> `worktree-setup.sh` still refuses to run `lake update`.

Consequence for `lake update`: it is not part of any automated path here. It
rewrites `lake-manifest.json`, which moves the cache key (§3) out from under
every published snapshot, and it mutates vendored package checkouts. Mathlib
bumps stay human-invoked, exactly as `update.yml:3-5` argues.

---

## 3. The cache key

```
keyhash := sha256( bytes(lean-toolchain) ‖ bytes(lake-manifest.json) ‖ bytes(lakefile.toml) )
```

concatenated in that fixed order, `‖` being byte concatenation. This is the local
analog of `hashFiles('lean-toolchain', 'lake-manifest.json', 'lakefile.toml')` in
`pr-ci.yml:143-149`. The definition is duplicated verbatim in `cache-warmer.sh`
and `warm-worktree.sh` (function `compute_keyhash`); the two copies **must stay
byte-identical**, or every consumer silently and permanently takes the cold path.
A missing input file is a hard error, never a default.

Two properties matter, and they are not symmetric:

1. **A snapshot may be older than the consumer's base commit.** The parent's
   `restore-keys` deliberately drop the SHA suffix and prefix-match the newest
   entry under the same hash. This is safe because Lake's staleness test is
   trace-hash based, not mtime based: a cloned artifact whose inputs still hash
   equal is reused, and everything else is rebuilt. Cloned files therefore do not
   need their timestamps preserved.
2. **A snapshot must never cross a keyhash boundary.** A `lean-toolchain` bump,
   a Mathlib revision change, or a `lakefile.toml` edit is *total* invalidation.
   `warm-worktree.sh` compares its own keyhash against the snapshot `STAMP`
   before copying anything, and on mismatch refuses the clone, warns, and falls
   back to the cold path. It never partially reuses.

## 4. On-disk layout

Shared packages and `hot-main` use `MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT`; branch products may
use `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` as in §2. Neither runtime tree is committed.

```
~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/
├── .full-build-lock/            # machine-wide: one full `lake build` at a time
│   └── info                     # pid, host, started, started_epoch, purpose
├── .telemetry-lock/             # short-lived; serializes JSONL appends
├── logs/                        # captured build logs (warm-*.log, worktree-build-*.log)
└── hot-main/
    ├── .writer-lease/           # only the warmer holds this
    │   └── info
    ├── repo/                    # the always-warm detached checkout of main
    ├── snapshots/
    │   ├── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
    │   │   ├── STAMP
    │   │   └── build/           # a byte copy of repo/.lake/build
    │   └── snap-<utc>-<sha12>/
    └── current -> snapshots/snap-<utc>-<sha12>   # absolute symlink
```

Snapshot names are `snap-<YYYYmmddTHHMMSSZ>-<sha12>` so that reverse
lexicographic order *is* reverse chronological order — the GC needs no `stat`
calls and no name parsing.

### `STAMP` schema

A flat `key=value` file, one pair per line. It is **data, not code**: both scripts
parse it with a whitelist and validate each value (`keyhash` must be 64 lowercase
hex characters, `status ∈ {complete, partial}`, `sha` hex). Nothing in it is ever
`eval`ed or `source`d.

```
sha=<full 40-char commit sha of the build>
keyhash=<64 hex chars, §3>
timestamp=<ISO 8601 with offset>
timestamp_epoch=<unix seconds>
status=complete|partial
build_seconds=<integer>
toolchain=<contents of lean-toolchain>
snapshot=<snapshot directory name>
warmer_version=1
```

## 5. The warmer — `cache-warmer.sh`

```
local/bin/cache-warmer.sh [--ref main | --sha <sha>] [--force] [--keep N]
                          [--targets "<lake targets>"] [--lock-timeout S]
                          [--lease-ttl S] [--gc-only] [--status]
```

### 5.1 Writer lease

Acquired by `mkdir hot-main/.writer-lease` — `mkdir(2)` is the atomic
test-and-set. The lease directory holds an `info` file with `pid`, `host`,
`started`, `started_epoch`, `purpose`.

Staleness is decided in this order:

* **Same host**: the holder's liveness is authoritative (`kill -0 pid`). A dead
  pid means stale immediately; a live pid means *not* stale regardless of age.
* **Different host, or no pid**: fall back to age > TTL (default 43200 s).

The TTL is deliberately much larger than the study map's suggested 3 h: this
repository's own cold full build took **25052 s** (`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`,
2026-08-30). An age-only rule with a short TTL would break a live warmer's lease
mid-build and produce exactly the concurrent-writer situation the lease exists to
prevent.

**Breaking a stale lock is done by renaming, not deleting.** Two processes that
both judge a lock stale will both attempt `mv lockdir lockdir.stale.<pid>.<epoch>`;
`rename(2)` is atomic, so exactly one succeeds and proceeds to delete and
re-acquire, while the loser loops and finds the lock freshly held. A
`rm -rf && mkdir` sequence has no such guarantee.

### 5.2 Build

1. Clone or fetch `hot-main/repo` from the primary checkout; resolve `origin/<ref>`
   first, then `<ref>` (`DESIGN.md` #8). Check out **detached** and forced.
   `.lake/` is gitignored, so the checkout never touches the build tree, and
   `git clean` is deliberately not run (it would descend into vendored packages).
2. Apply the fresh-state workaround (§8.2).
3. Acquire the machine-wide full-build lock (§7) — **waiting, never aborting.**
   This is the local reading of `pr-ci.yml:50`: a main build seeds the cache and
   is never cancelled in favour of a newer commit. If main moves during a build,
   finish, then warm again.
4. `lake exe cache get` (failure is a warning, not fatal — the build simply
   compiles more from source), then `lake build`, then any `--targets`.
   **No `lake update`.**
5. Everything is logged to `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/logs/warm-<utc>-<sha12>.log`.
   Telemetry records the log *path*, never log *content* — build output is
   untrusted text (`DESIGN.md` #6) and does not belong in a data file that agent
   prompts may later read.

### 5.3 Atomic publish

The publish sequence, and the reason each step is in this order:

1. Copy `repo/.lake/build` into `snapshots/<name>.tmp/build` with
   `cp -c -R` (APFS copy-on-write; falls back to `cp -R` with a warning if the
   source and destination are not on the same APFS volume).
2. Write `snapshots/<name>.tmp/STAMP`.
3. `mv snapshots/<name>.tmp snapshots/<name>` — a same-directory `rename(2)`.
   A snapshot directory therefore becomes visible only when it is already
   complete and stamped. **A reader can never observe a torn snapshot.**
4. Re-point `current` by creating a sibling symlink and `os.replace`-ing it over
   the old one (`rename(2)` again, which does not follow symlinks).

> Step 4 is done through `python3`, not `mv`. BSD `mv` `stat()`s its destination,
> follows the existing `current` symlink to the directory it names, and would
> move the new link *inside* the snapshot instead of replacing it. This is a real
> trap, not a hypothetical one.

Consumers exploit exactly this: they `readlink current` **once**, and hold the
resolved concrete path for the rest of the run.

### 5.4 Partial snapshots are intentional

If `lake build` fails, the warmer still publishes, with `status=partial`, and
exits non-zero. This is `pr-ci.yml:161-162` ported directly: a broken `main`
commit must not stall every consumer at zero cache, and the modules that did
compile are still worth distributing. Consumers accept partial snapshots and say
so loudly.

A non-zero exit from the warmer therefore means *"main did not build cleanly"* —
not *"nothing was published."* A cron wrapper should treat it as an alert, not a
reason to retry.

### 5.5 Retention

Keep the newest `--keep` snapshots (default 2), the local analog of the parent's
10 GB repository cache budget. **The snapshot `current` points to is never
collected**, even when it falls outside the keep window: a consumer that has
resolved `current` must find a live directory. Abandoned `*.tmp` staging
directories older than an hour are swept.

Elimination: prove\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\n```\n\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\ndeviation has been discharged.\n\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker.  If the paper\nhas a local typo, a documented numerical strengthening, or a genuine scope\nrestriction, use a lighter docstring marker such as `**Local fix:**` or\n`**Scope restriction:**`, citing the relevant paper-gap note.  These lighter\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\npaper hypotheses.\n\n## Code Conventions\n\n### Imports\n\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\n- One import per line\n- Follow existing local import style\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\n\n### File structure\n\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\n\n1. imports\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\n3. namespace / opens / variables\n4. declarations\n\n### Formatting\n\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\n  own line\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\n  theorem statement\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\n  tactic blocks.\n\n### Naming conventions\n\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\n\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\n\nProject-preferred variable names:\n\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\n- `σ` — strategies\n- `P` — projective measurements\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\n\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\n\n### Types and signatures\n\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\n  wrappers\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\n\n### Documentation\n\nRequired:\n\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\n- Cite blueprint nodes by their stable LaTeX label, for example blueprint\n  `lem:cl-concat`. Do not store blueprint line numbers in Lean docstrings. When\n  reviewing, derive the current span with\n  `python3 scripts/blueprint_citations.py resolve lem:cl-concat`.\n- Cite paper mirrors by a paper label when one exists, or by a repository path\n  plus a narrow anchored passage when the source has no suitable label. Paper\n  mirror line ranges are acceptable because those mirrors are immutable.\n\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\lean{...}`\nand `\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\n\n## Proof Engineering\n\n### Search before proving\n\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\n\n### Mathlib integration\n\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\n\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\n\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\n\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\n\n### Validation ladder\n\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\n2. `lake build`\n\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\n\n### Lean-specific advice\n\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\n  already in the repo\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\n\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\n\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\nmathematical phrase is available.\n\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\npaper, and the local formalization. An\nabsolute `MIPSTARRE_LAKE_ROOT` may instead hold branch-private `.lake` products.\n\n## GitHub → local mapping\n\n| GitHub mechanism | Local replacement |\n|---|---|\n| PR CI (`pr-ci.yml`) on push/PR events | `local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id>` run by the PR lifecycle scripts |\n| Main-build actions cache (main-only save, PR restore) | Hot main cache: single-writer warmer + read-only snapshots + APFS copy-on-write clones per worktree (`build-cache.md`) |\n| `lake exe cache get` (Mathlib cloud cache) | Unchanged — already local |\n| Model-backed PR review chained on CI success | `local/bin/review.sh <pr-number>`: codex CLI with the same `.github/prompts/` review personas, invoked only from green exact-head CI statuses; one COMMENT review plus `local-review/summary` |\n| Auto-fix workflows (CI-fix, blueprint-fix, review-fix) | `local/bin/autofix.sh <pr-id> --mode {ci,blueprint,review,auto}` with the same commit-prefix guards and a combined iteration cap |\n| `@claude`/`@codex` mention responders | `local/bin/agent.sh <id> \"instruction\"` — human-invoked codex session on the branch worktree |\n| GitHub issues + sub-issues + labels | unchanged — GitHub is the record again (`issues-prs.md`); `issue_new.py` / `issue_close.py` drive it through `gh_common.py` |\n| GitHub PRs | GitHub PRs, branch-per-issue, merge gate in `pr_merge.py` (REST merge with the exact-SHA guard) |\n| Issue automation (classify/scout/track/followups) | `local/bin/` Python ports; LLM steps optional behind `MIPSTARRE_LLM_ENABLED` |\n| Housekeeping crons (standup, stale audit, linter sweep, README freshness) | `local/bin/housekeeping.sh <job>` on demand |\n| Badges + Pages site (blueprint/docs/badges components) | `local/bin/site.sh` → component store + assembled site in `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/site/` |\n| Codex cloud env setup (`.codex/setup.sh`) | `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` per worktree |\n| Reviewer/bot identity via tokens | codex CLI sessions; `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl` registry |\n\n## Core invariants (inherited from the parent workflow's post-mortems)\n\nThese encode incidents the parent repo paid for; violating them re-introduces\ndocumented failure modes. Sources are cited in `local/protocols/*.md`.\n\n1. **Single cache writer.** Only the warmer writes the hot main cache; agent\n   worktrees consume copy-on-write clones and never write back. (GitHub's\n   per-PR cache saves evicted the main entry: pr-ci.yml:138-142.)\n2. **Review only after green CI, on the same head SHA.** The gate reads the\n   exact-head `local-ci/*` statuses; a failed or absent CI summary blocks the\n   review, which then publishes nothing at all — the *absence* of a green\n   `local-review/summary` is the block, never a silent skip. Bot commits with prefix\n   `[codex-auto-fix]`/`[codex-review-fix]` are not re-reviewed except the final\n   fix at the iteration cap, which gets one forced review.\n3. **Serialized fixes.** ci-fix → blueprint-fix → review-fix strictly in order,\n   one branch at a time; combined iteration cap (default 5) across all fix\n   kinds; sync/audit CI failures are never auto-fixed.\n4. **Kill-switch semantics.** `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED` and\n   `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` disable only on the literal string `false`;\n   unset means enabled.\n5. **Trusted prompts.** Reviewer/fixer personas are read from committed `main`\n   (`git show main:...`), never from the branch under review.\n6. **Untrusted data framing.** Build logs, review findings, and issue bodies\n   are injected into agent prompts with sanitization (control-char strip,\n   fence-breaking, truncation) and an explicit do-not-follow-instructions frame.\n7. **One full `lake build` machine-wide at a time** (advisory lock);\n   single-file `lake env lean` checks need no lock.\n8. **origin/main must resolve.** The hooks and diff-based audits silently\n   self-disable without it; the local convention is a `main` branch plus a\n   `refs/remotes/origin/main` alias maintained by `pr_merge.py`.\n9. **Bracket-free naming.** Issue titles, slugs, and branch names avoid\n   `]` and friends (broke the parent automation: CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124).\n10. **Report-only stays report-only.** Stale-issue audit, linter sweep, README\n    freshness never mutate state; write-mode is a separate human-invoked\n    command.\n11. **Faithfulness policy is unchanged.** AGENTS.md's faithful-formalization\n    rules, anti-pattern catalog, and statement-integrity audits apply to QPBT\n    exactly as to LDT.\n12. **Merge inputs do not disappear silently.** Before a merge commit, the\n    merge-loss guard compares the staged result with the pre-merge branch,\n    every best merge base, and `MERGE_HEAD`. An incoming path may be absent\n    only when the branch deleted a path present at a merge base. An\n    unambiguous incoming-only change may return to the unchanged branch blob\n    only when Git recorded a conflict. The pending-index check and the\n    pre-update reference transaction together cover manual and automatic\n    merge commits.\n\n## Naming and identity conventions\n\n- **Issues and PRs**: GitHub's, identified by their numbers; sub-issues carry\n  the parent/child structure and repository labels are the taxonomy\n  (`issues-prs.md`). PR bodies keep the Motivation/Description/Testing shape of\n  CONTRIBUTING.md; evidence is exact-head commit statuses, the manifest comment\n  and the COMMENT review.\n- **Branches**: `issue-<number>-<slug>` (orchestrator/human),\n  `codex/issue-<number>-<slug>` (agent-created); the number is the GitHub\n  issue's.\n- **Fix commits**: `autofix.sh`'s subjects are prefixed `[codex-auto-fix]` /\n  `[codex-review-fix]` exactly (the review-gate skip regex depends on them);\n  operator and worker repairs use plain `fix(...)` subjects and are reviewed.\n- **Codex sessions**: `<role>-<issue|scope>-<yyyymmdd>-<seq>` with roles\n  `orc, prover, reviewer, simplifier, blueprint, splitter, scout`, plus\n  `mathfix` for astra after its availability is reported on #26.\n  External sessions use `local/bin/dispatch.sh`, which records the codex `thread_id`,\n  captures the `--json` event stream to\n  `results/telemetry/sessions/<name>.jsonl`, and appends a summary line to\n  `results/telemetry/sessions.jsonl`. Archiving a session = final status line\n  in the registry + worktree removal; the JSONL capture is the archive. Complements\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\nbake in*.\n\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\n\n- Be marked `\\leanok` in the blueprint,\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\n\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\nbranch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this\ncodebase.\n\n## Catalogue\n\n- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)\n- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)\n- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)\n- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)\n- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)\n- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)\n\n---\n\n## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis\n\n**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own\nconclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\nPR [#491].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\n\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\nconclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. If the missing content\ncannot be formalized yet, state the missing assertion as a named obligation\nto be proved from the paper hypotheses, and leave the corresponding proof open\nunder a tracker. Do not put that obligation on the source-labelled theorem as\nan extra hypothesis. Existing `BridgePackage`-style declarations are proof\ndebt to be removed or converted into source-faithful obligations; they are not\nthe preferred shape for new work.\n\nA signature passes the smell test if:\n\n- Every hypothesis is a **named intermediate fact** that also appears in the\n  paper or blueprint proof, not the theorem's output packaged up, and\n- Replacing a hypothesis with its negation would produce a *different*\n  theorem, not a trivially-false one.\n\n### Related issues and patterns\n\n- [#449] — paper-wide gap tracker\n- [#451] — the tracked `BridgePackage` producer catalogue\n- [#595] — resolved the QXP `ProjectiveNonMeasurementBridgePackage` offender by\n  deleting the bridge and threading `RoundingToProjectorsWitness` directly\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` axiom-field projection (a definitional variant)\n- [#493] — the inline-existential mutation of this pattern\n- [#491] — PR that introduced the mutation\n\n---\n\n## A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand\n\n**Smell.** A `def`/`abbrev` is written so its body is the paper's claim, and\na nearby `theorem` restates that claim and proves it by `rfl` (or a one-line\n`simp [foo]` where `foo` is the defining equation). The \"mathematical\ncontent\" has been baked into the definition; the theorem is a tautology. See\nissues [#477], [#494].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\n`rfl` proves that a definition equals itself. If the definition is chosen\n*so that* it equals the conclusion, the `rfl` \"proof\" transports none of the\npaper's reasoning — it is literally the reflexivity of a shape we invented to\nmatch the conclusion. The real identity the paper proves (e.g.,\n`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ` over an actual inner product) is still not stated\nanywhere in Lean.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- A `theorem` whose body is `rfl` / `by rfl` / `by simp [defName]` where\n  `defName` is the def that unfolds to the conclusion.\n- A `structure` with a `Prop`-typed field whose *role* in the paper is a\n  nontrivial identity (SVD, orthonormality, Cauchy–Schwarz), accompanied by a\n  constructor that discharges that field with `rfl`.\n- A `def foo := if α = β then 1 else 0` followed by a theorem asserting\n  `foo α β = if α = β then 1 else 0`.\n- Bridge-like structures where every field is itself a function\n  `(precondition) → (conclusion-step)` and the consumer applies the field\n  directly.\n\n### Concrete example\n\nFrom `MIPStarRE/LDT/ExpansionHypercubeGraph/Defs/Fourier.lean`:\n\n```lean\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\ndef fourierBasisInnerProduct (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) : Error :=\n  if α = β then 1 else 0\n\n/-- The exact inner-product formula for the hypercube Fourier basis. -/\nlemma fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq (params : Parameters)\n    (α β : Point params) :\n    fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0 := rfl\n\n/-- `prop:eigenvectors`. -/\ntheorem eigenvectors (params : Parameters) :\n    (∀ α β : Point params,\n      fourierBasisInnerProduct params α β = if α = β then 1 else 0) ∧ ... := by\n  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩\n  · intro α β\n    exact fourierBasisInnerProduct_eq params α β    -- castle: def IS Kronecker delta\n  ...\n```\n\nThe paper's orthonormality claim — that the additive characters `φ_α` form an\northonormal basis under the actual inner product\n`⟨f, g⟩ := (1/|V|) · ∑_u f(u)^* · g(u)` — requires a genuine character-sum\nidentity. The Lean theorem states and proves only the trivial fact that the\ndefinition equals itself.\n\n### Not every `rfl` is a castle\n\nDistinguish from legitimate bookkeeping where a named equation is literally\nhow something was defined. Example: `mainFormalError_eq_envelope` in\n`Test/ErrorCascade/Definitions.lean` unfolds the definition of\n`mainFormalError` to its envelope factorization. The mathematical content is\nelsewhere (the envelope is derived from per-step bounds); the `rfl` theorem is\na naming convenience only. The test is: **does the `def` body encode a paper\nidentity, or does it just name a compound expression?**\n\n### How to fix it\n\n1. Move the paper's real definition to the concrete one: for Fourier, define\n   the inner product as the actual sum over vertices, and the characters\n   `φ_α` as functions from `Point params` to `ℂ`.\n2. State the paper's identity (`⟨φ_α, φ_β⟩ = δ_αβ`) as a theorem over those\n   concrete objects.\n3. Prove it via the standard character-sum derivation (or cite the Mathlib\n   counterpart if one exists — `Matrix.dotProduct` / `Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff`\n   combined with `ZMod.sum_pow_units` style lemmas).\n4. If you want to keep the Kronecker shorthand, define it *afterward* as a\n   consequence, not as the primitive.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#477] — resolved `QXPLayerData` field projections (Ch4 SVD as axiom fields)\n- [#494] — the Fourier case and other candidates\n\n---\n\n## A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions\n\n**Smell.** A total function is defined by `if eligible then real_value else\ndefault`, where the `default` (usually `0`, `default`, `⊥`, or\n`Classical.arbitrary`) is a sentinel for \"precondition not met.\" Downstream\ntheorems state properties that are only true on the eligible branch, but the\ntheorem's type signature does not carry the eligibility proof, so the\nobligation moves silently from the prover to whoever happens to call the\nfunction. See issue [#495], related to [#307].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe signature lies about the domain of validity. A caller passing a\nnon-eligible input gets `0` back; any theorem proved about \"the output\" is\nproved for `0`, which is trivially true and carries no information. When a\nlater theorem composes the output with another lemma, the composition\ntype-checks but the conclusion is vacuous on inputs where the original\nprecondition failed.\n\nThe paper, by contrast, restricts the quantifier in the first place:\n\"Fix a tuple `(x₁, ..., x_k)` with Hamming weight `≥ d+1`.\" The Lean should\nmatch.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- `match ... with | some _ => real | none => 0` or `| _ => 0`.\n- `if hEligible : P then ... else default`.\n- Identifier names containing `fallback`, `placeholder`, `sentinel`,\n  `dummy`, `or0`, `orDefault`.\n- Recursive definitions whose base case unconditionally returns a sentinel.\n- Functions that return `Polynomial params` but can return the zero polynomial\n  on inputs that shouldn't be in the domain.\n\n### Concrete example (historical; resolved by PR #561)\n\nUntil PR #561, `MIPStarRE/LDT/Pasting/Defs/Interpolation.lean` contained:\n\n```lean\n/-- Extract the polynomial from a completed slice outcome; returns 0 on ⊥. -/\nnoncomputable def extractSliceOr0 {params : Parameters} [FieldModel params.q]\n    (g : GHatOutcome params) : PolynomialModel params :=\n  match g with\n  | some p => p.poly\n  | none   => 0\n```\n\nThe consumer `interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport` ran Lagrange\ninterpolation on `extractSliceOr0`-extracted values. If the support contained\na `none`, the interpolant silently pretended that slice evaluated to zero.\nThe paper's Lagrange step is quantified over *eligible* slices only, so the\nLean API should carry `∀ i ∈ support, (g i).isSome` as a hypothesis; instead\nit carried nothing, and the theorem technically type-checked on inputs for\nwhich its conclusion was meaningless.\n\n**Current status:** resolved. The live API now removes `extractSliceOr0`,\nthreads the explicit hypothesis `hσsupport : σ ⊆ gHatTupleSupport gs` into\n`interpolateCompletedSlicesFromSupport`, and packages the chosen support subset\nas `InterpolationSupportWitness` so the arbitrary choice and its proof fields\nare visible at call sites.\n\n### Acceptable uses of this pattern\n\nNot every default branch is a castle. `Inhabited` / `Nonempty` instances\nthat provide a canonical inhabitant (e.g., the zero polynomial for\n`Nonempty (Polynomial params)`) are plumbing, not proof. The test is: **does\nany theorem mention the output?** If a theorem says \"the output satisfies\nP\", and P is not trivially satisfied by the sentinel, the fallback is\nsmuggling a precondition.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPick one of:\n\n1. **Make the precondition explicit.** Add `(h : eligible input) :` to the\n   signature. Let Lean's type system enforce that non-eligible inputs cannot\n   be passed.\n2. **Return an `Option`.** The `none` result forces every caller to handle\n   the case, so theorems about \"the output\" now quantify only over the\n   `some` branch.\n3. **Restrict the domain.** Instead of `(x : X) → Y`, take `(x : {x : X //\n   P x}) → Y`. Common for finite-support Lagrange-style constructions where\n   the subtype is computable via `Finset.filter`.\n\n### Classical-logic dependencies\n\nA sibling smell in this pattern: `DecidablePred` / `DecidableEq` instances\nthat silently use `Classical.dec` to fill in decidability that should be\nconstructive. The historical `interpolationEligibleSandwichFamily`\nimplementation was exactly such a case: it used `open Classical in ...` to\ngate a predicate that is actually decidable by a finite-support check. PR\n#561 fixed that example by adding `interpolationEligible_decidablePred`.\nThose classical instances are acceptable only when the predicate is genuinely\nnon-constructive; if a constructive instance is plausible, write it, don't\nbottom out in `Classical.dec`. See [#495] for the full catalogue of\nclassical-logic uses in `LDT/Pasting/`.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#307] — placeholder Lagrange coefficient (original fallback tracker)\n- [#495] — the full pasting-interpolation catalogue\n\n---\n\n## A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials\n\n**Smell.** A theorem of the shape `∃ x, P x` is closed by picking\n`x := default`, `x := 0`, `x := 1`, or `x := Classical.arbitrary`, where the\npaper names a *specific, non-trivial* `x` and derives `P x` from real\nstructure. The Lean claim is *mathematically* weaker because the Lean\ntheorem guarantees less than the paper's (it proves some-trivial-thing, not\nthe-specific-paper-thing). See [#449] for the full ledger.\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem name matches a paper lemma but the witness has been cheapened\ninto a placeholder. Downstream theorems that inspect the witness get `0` or\n`default`, which is almost always useless. Consumers that \"use\" the lemma\nare really using the trivial `∃` and cannot proceed past the first attempt\nto pin the witness down.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- `refine ⟨default, ?_⟩` / `exact ⟨default, ...⟩` / `refine ⟨0, ?_⟩` /\n  `exact ⟨1, ...⟩` inside a proof of a paper-cited existential.\n- `letI : Inhabited X := ⟨Classical.arbitrary X⟩` followed by a `let x :=\n  default`.\n- `Classical.arbitrary` / `Classical.choice` / `Nonempty.some` in proof\n  bodies (as opposed to typeclass definitions).\n- Identifier suffix `...Witness := default` on a bundled output.\n\n### Concrete example\n\nFrom the ledger in [#449]:\n\n- `lem:sdp` / `sdp` — primal witness is `T := default` (a zero\n  submeasurement) and dual witness `Z := 1`. The paper requires a specific\n  feasible pair; the Lean version proves only that some arbitrary pair exists,\n  which always does.\n- `lem:projective-low-rank-sum` / `projectiveLowRankSum` — auxiliary\n  projective measurement `t := (default : ProjMeas Outcome ι)`. The paper\n  constructs `(auxSpace, T_a)` from the eigenvector basis of each rounded\n  `R_a`; the Lean version picks a zero-dimensional placeholder, which is\n  disconnected from the paper's SVD derivation.\n- ~~`lem:global-rewrite` / `globalRewrite` — decomposition witness is\n  `default`~~ (historical; resolved by PRs #527 and #542). The live theorem now\n  uses `canonicalGlobalVarianceDecomposition`, and\n  `globalVarianceTraceWitness` consumes the centered residual family\n  `u ↦ A^u - A_{\\mathrm{avg}}` rather than ignoring the witness.\n\n### Acceptable uses\n\nNon-computable instances required for typeclass plumbing, such as\n`Nonempty (Polynomial params)` inhabited by the zero polynomial, are fine when\nthey are used only to *inhabit* a type, not to discharge a paper-cited\nexistential.  Degenerate measurements should be constructed explicitly with a\nspecified outcome rather than supplied by an ambient `Inhabited` instance.  The\nsmell is specifically about `default` showing up in the proof of a *theorem\nnamed after a paper result*.\n\n### How to fix it\n\n- Construct the paper's witness explicitly. If the ingredients are not yet\n  formalized (e.g., Mathlib SVD, spectral decomposition), extract a bridge\n  lemma that *constructs* the witness from the missing Mathlib facts, and\n  track the Mathlib gap as a separate issue.\n- Keep the existential statement, but strengthen the conclusion so that\n  `x := default` no longer satisfies it (e.g., \"there exists `x` *with*\n  rank `m`\", not merely \"there exists `x`\").\n- If the witness cannot yet be constructed, keep the source-facing existential\n  statement and expose the missing construction as a named proof obligation.\n  Replacing `default` by an explicit bridge hypothesis is still an A1-grade\n  placeholder, not a proof of the paper theorem.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#449] — master ledger; all three known cases are already listed\n\n---\n\n## A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib\n\n**Smell.** Lean code re-declares or re-proves something that already lives\nin Mathlib, or builds a tower of custom lemmas that never bottom out in\nMathlib / Lean core. The proof \"works\" only because the internal custom\nstatements are compatible with each other — it is a closed ecosystem that\ndoesn't ground in the reference library.\n\nThis is the \"scaffolding that blocks real formalization\" section of\n[`project_conventions.md`](./project_conventions.md) in concrete examples. The two\nflavours:\n\n1. **Re-proving Mathlib.** Writing `private lemma my_add_comm : a + b = b + a`\n   when `add_comm` exists.\n2. **Custom types that shadow Mathlib.** Defining `MyMeasurement` instead of\n   using `MeasureTheory.Measure`, `MyMatrix` instead of `Matrix`,\n   `MyHermitian` instead of `Matrix.IsHermitian`. The custom version may be\n   definitionally equal to (or coercible from) the Mathlib version, but if\n   it isn't, every consumer must reprove everything.\n\n### Why it's bad\n\n1. The duplicated statements aren't audited by Mathlib's community, so they\n   may be subtly wrong (wrong edge case, wrong universe, wrong typeclass).\n2. When the real Mathlib proof is needed (for a key gap lemma), the custom\n   tower must be rewritten to interoperate — often via a painful coercion\n   layer that reintroduces every fact.\n3. Hides real Mathlib gaps. If we decline to use Mathlib because \"our\n   version is simpler,\" the gap never gets filed against Mathlib.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- `private lemma` in a file about well-established algebra/analysis\n  (Cauchy–Schwarz, `sqrt`, `rpow`, `PosSemidef`, `Matrix.trace`, etc.).\n- Custom structures named `MyX` / `LocalX` / `ProjectX` where `X` is a\n  standard concept.\n- Proof bodies that chain ten `private lemma`s where the natural Mathlib\n  counterpart would be two `exact?` lookups.\n- Files with no `import Mathlib.*` above the level of `Mathlib.Tactic.*`\n  when the subject matter is clearly Mathlib-adjacent (linear algebra,\n  analysis, measure theory).\n\n### How to fix it\n\nBefore writing a new lemma, spend one minute on:\n\n- `exact?` / `apply?` on the goal.\n- `#find` / `Loogle` for the statement shape.\n- `rg -n \"theorem.*X\" .lake/packages/mathlib/` for a keyword.\n\nIf Mathlib has it, use it. If it doesn't, consider whether the missing\nlemma should be upstreamed (file an issue against Mathlib, or at least a\nTODO pointing at the gap). The project already has this mandate — see the\n\"Mathlib Integration\" section of [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md):\n\n> Scout Mathlib first (`exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source)\n\nA5 is what happens when that step is skipped.\n\n### Audit cross-reference\n\n`audits/` contains chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency scouting\nreports. If a section of the code review says \"this could use Mathlib\nlemma X\", it belongs in a specific `audits/*.md` file for that chapter.\n\n---\n\n## A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles\n\n**Smell.** A theorem takes a hypothesis of type `SomeStatement` (or\n`SomeWitness`, `SomeOutput`, etc.) that is defined elsewhere and intended\nto represent an external mathematical result, but there is no theorem\nconstructing it from the hypotheses under which the paper uses it. The Lean\nstatement is then:\n\"assuming the external result, the Lean conclusion holds.\" That is\nsometimes legitimate (e.g., a cite to a book whose formalization we don't\nplan to do), and sometimes a cover for locally-unwanted work.\n\nThis overlaps with A1 but is subtler: the hypothesis isn't the\n*current theorem's* conclusion, it's an *independently-named* claim that\nhappens to unblock the current proof.\n\n### Acceptable external smuggles\n\n- **Genuine external citations.** `PolishchukSpielmanClassicalSoundnessStatement`\n  cites the Polishchuk–Spielman theorem; we don't plan to formalize it.\n- **Mathlib gaps we can't fill.** `hMatrixChernoff` in `chernoffBernoulliMatrix`\n  is a Mathlib matrix-Chernoff-type statement; we flagged the gap upstream.\n- **Tracked internal obligations.** A `*Statement` that has an open sub-issue\n  and a named construction theorem target is trackable proof debt. It is still\n  not an acceptable extra hypothesis on a source-labelled paper theorem.\n\n### Unacceptable external smuggles\n\n- A `*Statement` with no open tracking issue, no docstring explaining the\n  mathematical gap, and no consumer-side comment flagging the smuggle.\n- A `*Statement` whose body is the theorem's conclusion, wearing a different\n  name (A1 in disguise).\n- A `*Statement` used to close a lemma whose paper version does not require\n  any such external assumption (silent strengthening of the Lean theorem\n  relative to the paper's).\n\n### How to spot it\n\nGrep for these suffixes: `*Statement`, `*Witness`, `*Claim`,\n`*Conclusion`, `*Output`, `*Input`, `*Hypothesis`, `*Requirement`,\n`*Assumption`, `*Package` (that isn't a `*BridgePackage`). For each, ask:\n\n- Is there a theorem anywhere that **constructs** a value of this type from the\n  paper hypotheses?\n- If not, is the absence explained in a docstring / tracking issue /\n  `audits/` entry?\n- Does the paper depend on an external theorem of this shape?\n\nIf any answer is \"no\", the structure is an unacceptable smuggle.\n\n### Current status (audited 2026-05-08)\n\nThe May 2026 re-audit\n([`audits/2026-05-08_statement-smuggle-reaudit.md`](../blob/main/audits/2026-05-08_statement-smuggle-reaudit.md))\nclassified 39 `*Statement` structures (102 declarations total across the\nextended suffix sweep of `*Witness`/`*Conclusion`/`*Input`/etc.).\n\nThe live ledger is [#1379], replacing the now-closed [#449] (2026-05-01) and\n[#451] (2026-04-30). Headline counts from the re-audit: 33 grounded, 2 tracked\nsmuggle, 2 external citation, 1 paper-faithful packaging, 1 dead. Without a live\nledger, **5 `*Statement` structures landed between 2026-04-18 and 2026-05-08\nwithout a tracker entry** — the gap this policy fixes.\n\nThe Section 5 spectral-truncation chain is now an example of the preferred\nmigration: the old `SpectralTruncationInput` abbreviation has been removed, and\nlater arguments call direct constructors for `SpectralTruncationStatement`\ninstead of carrying an `Input` wrapper.\n\nIf you add a new `*Statement`-style structure to this codebase, include a\ndef-site docstring with its paper origin (per the \"earn your place\" policy in\n[#1379]). If no construction theorem exists yet, file a sub-issue in [#1379]\nand ship the source-faithful construction theorem with an explicit unfinished\nproof obligation. Do not add the structure as a new source-theorem hypothesis\nmerely to keep downstream declarations compiling.\n\n### Merge gate — new `*Statement` / `*Witness` / `*Input` structures\n\nTo prevent dead scaffolds from landing unnoticed (the 5-structure gap of\n2026-04-18–2026-05-08), every PR that introduces a new `structure XStatement`,\n`structure XWitness`, `structure XInput`, `abbrev XStatement`, or\n`abbrev XInput` must satisfy **at least one** of these before merge:\n\n1. **Has a construction theorem.** A theorem that constructs a value of this\n   type from the appropriate paper hypotheses appears in the same PR or an\n   already-merged ancestor. If the proof is not finished, the theorem must carry\n   the explicit tracked proof obligation rather than moving the assertion into a\n   paper-facing theorem's hypotheses.\n2. **Has a consumer.** A theorem that takes a value of this type as a\n   hypothesis appears in the same PR or an already-merged ancestor.\n3. **Has a ledger entry.** A classification comment (G / E / T / P / D, per\n   the verdict key in [#1379]) is posted on [#1379] as an issue comment, and\n   the structure's def-site docstring links to that comment.\n\nStructures that satisfy none of the above are dead on arrival and must not\nmerge.\n\n### Related issues\n\n- [#1379] — live `*Statement` ledger (replaces closed [#449] / [#451])\n- [#449] — historical paper-wide gap tracker (closed 2026-05-01)\n- [#451] — historical bridge-hypothesis tracker (closed 2026-04-30)\n- [#278] — the original \"derive `PermInvState` internally\" discussion\n\n---\n\n## Reviewer checklist\n\nUse this alongside the blocker\nlist in the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and the [`proof_frontier_review.md`](./proof_frontier_review.md)\nchecklist for structure fields. For any theorem or lemma that claims a paper\nresult, ask:\n\n- [ ] **Hypothesis audit.** Does any hypothesis contain (up to `∃`/`∧`) the\n      theorem's conclusion? If yes, that's A1 — reject or strengthen.\n- [ ] **Definitional audit.** Is the proof `rfl` or a one-line `simp`? If\n      yes, does the unfolded definition do the paper's math, or just match\n      the shape of the conclusion? The latter is A2.\n- [ ] **Domain audit.** Does the function have a fallback branch (`if\n      eligible ... else default`)? If yes, does the theorem's signature\n      require eligibility? If not, that's A3.\n- [ ] **Witness audit.** Does the proof pick `x := default` for an\n      existential named after a paper lemma? That's A4 unless the witness\n      is genuinely unique-up-to-isomorphism.\n- [ ] **Mathlib audit.** Is there a `private lemma` that duplicates a\n      Mathlib fact? Run `exact?` / `apply?` / `#find` before accepting it\n      (A5).\n- [ ] **External-citation audit.** Does the proof consume a `*Statement` /\n      `*Witness` / `*Package`? Is there a tracking issue that names its\n      grounding plan (A6)?\n- [ ] **Paper-faithfulness.** Does the Lean signature match the paper's\n      statement, or does Lean sneak in extra hypotheses? Flag divergences\n      as ⚠️S in [#1379].\n\nA lemma that passes all of these is a proof.
